title: How AI turns words into numbers
label: EP 28
banner: How AI turns words into numbers

yt.title: What ChatGPT actually sees
notes: You type: 'The Statue of Liberty is in'
No words, only numbers (real token IDs)

lines.text: To ChatGPT, your message looks like [1] this. [2] No words, only numbers. [3] So how does it turn these numbers into an answer?

yt.title: Step 1: cut the text into tokens
notes: A token is a word or a piece of a word
Each token gets an ID, like a ticket number

lines.text: First, your text is cut into tokens, [1] words or pieces of words. [2] Even 'YouTube' is two tokens. [3] Each token gets an ID, but an ID is just a label, like a ticket number.
lines.tts: First, your text is cut into tokens, words or pieces of words. Even YouTube is two tokens. Each token gets an I.D., but an I.D. is just a label, like a ticket number.

yt.title: Step 2: IDs become embeddings
notes: Each ID fetches its row from a giant table
Google Maps places you with 2 numbers

lines.text: So [1] each ID fetches its row from a giant table: a long list of numbers, called an embedding. [2] It's an address: Google Maps places you with two numbers, [3] an embedding uses thousands. [4] Similar meanings live nearby, so 'cat' sits next to 'dog'.
lines.show: So [1] each ID fetches its row from a giant table: a long list of numbers, called an embedding. [2] It's an address: Google Maps places you with 2 numbers, [3] an embedding uses thousands. [4] Similar meanings live nearby, so 'cat' sits next to 'dog'.
lines.tts: So each I.D. fetches its row from a giant table: a long list of numbers, called an embedding. It's an address: Google Maps places you with two numbers, an embedding uses thousands. Similar meanings live nearby, so cat sits next to dog.

yt.title: Position signals
notes: 'dog' gets the same embedding, first or last
Each token also carries its position

lines.text: But 'dog' gets the same list, first or last, [1] so 'dog bites man' would equal 'man bites dog'. [2] So each token also carries its position, [3] and now it knows who bit whom.
lines.tts: But dog gets the same list, first or last, so dog bites man would equal man bites dog. So each token also carries its position, and now it knows who bit whom.

yt.title: Step 3: climb the layers
notes: Each word looks back and soaks up what matters (attention, EP27)

lines.text: Then the embeddings climb dozens of layers. [1] On every floor, each word looks back and soaks up what matters. [2] By the top, the last word, 'in', knows about 'Statue' and 'Liberty'.
lines.tts: Then the embeddings climb dozens of layers. On every floor, each word looks back, and soaks up what matters. By the top, the last word, in, knows about Statue and Liberty.

yt.title: Step 4: one token at a time
notes: One trip per token = answers appear piece by piece

lines.text: Now it scores every possible next token, [1] picks a likely one, 'New', [2] and climbs again for [3] 'York'. One trip per token: that's why answers appear piece by piece.
lines.tts: Now it scores every possible next token, picks a likely one, New, and climbs again for York. One trip per token: that's why answers appear piece by piece.

yt.title: Same ID for 'bank'?
notes: Yes: same ID (6922), same starting embedding

lines.text: Your turn: [1] does 'bank' get the same ID in 'river bank' and 'bank account'? <pause 2> [2] Yes! Same ID, same starting list. The layers tell them apart.

yt.title: Words to numbers to answer
notes: Text -> tokens -> IDs -> embeddings -> layers -> next token

lines.text: In short: text, [1] tokens, [2] IDs, [3] embeddings, [4] layers, [5] then one token at a time. [6] Next: how AI sees images. Follow, so you don't miss it.
